newsitem.title: FINLAND: POHJOLA CEO CONFIDENT OF SUOMI RESHUFFLE.
newsitem.headline: POHJOLA CEO CONFIDENT OF SUOMI RESHUFFLE.

text.p: Finnish insurer Pohjola's CEO said on Thursday he was confident that policyholders in associated mutual insurer Suomi will approve a plan to shift Suomi's life insurance into Pohjola's hands.

"I have no reason to doubt that (the plan) wouldn't come about because the figures largely speak on its behalf," Pohjola president and CEO Iiro Viinanen, also chairman of Suomi, told Reuters after a news conference.
"The way this structural rearrangement will be carried out is undisputably to the benefit of policyholders," he said.
"Policyholders will benefit from the fact that we will be able to give better security and better returns on their insurance," Viinanen said.
Suomi's large solvency capital -- at 4.03 billion at end-1996 -- would be used to enable higher returns on current Suomi policy-holders insurance deposits, he said.
But Viinanen said the actual amount of capital earmarked was three billion.

"The surplus assets, or in other words the solvency capital of about three billion markka, is earmarked capital the returns on which will only be used to benefit the old insurance portfolio," Viinanen said.

The value of the portfolio to be transferred to Pohjola would depend on the market value of assets but based on last year's figures, it would be about three billion markka in solvency capital and almost seven billion in insurance, he said.

Representatives of policyholders in Suomi mutual will rule on the plan on May 6 and before that, the plan would come before the supervisory boards of Suomi and Pohjola, Viinanen said, but did not give dates for those meetings.
The transfer of Suomi's life insurance portfolio would take two or three years to complete, Suomi chief executive Jukka Rantala said, adding many technical matters were still open.
Suomi reported 1996 operating profits up 81 percent to 660 million markka from 364 million in 1995.
